title: Python rule (tests never touch the live .relay/queue)…
what: tests/test_queue.py:488: MEDIUM: F5 Python rule (tests never touch the live .relay/queue): several tests read the checkout's live queue, and test_f7 breaks with KeyError once the gate-log-summary feature is done
why: Found 26 Oct by the review of wt/tests-tmp (outside that change: it did not touch these tests). Breaks the project's Python rule "Tests use a temporary folder and never touch the live .relay/queue". A gate would go red on a queue event (an item moving to done/), not on a code change.
failing_case: tests/test_queue.py:488 reads committed_items(ROOT)["gate-log-summary.json"]; committed_items lists only the top level of
.relay/queue/ (not done/). When the owner's queue moves gate-log-summary to .relay/queue/done/ (the item is taken and
finished), the test raises KeyError and the gate goes red for a queue event, not a code change. Other live reads:
tests/test_queue.py:462 and :504 (every live item), :476-485 (git log of the live queue in ROOT),
tests/test_split_test_files.py:65 (live done item). Should: each reads a fixture copy in a temporary folder, or a
pass_cases: 1. With .relay/queue/gate-log-summary.json moved to .relay/queue/done/ in a scratch copy, tests/test_queue.py passes.
2. test_f7 still asserts kind feature, ip 0, no failing_case, on a fixed copy of the item.
